adText.description: Rates as low as 4.59% APR* on new and used autos. Members get 0.65% off your rate with autopay.

modelAnswer.description: Rates as low as 4.59% APR* on new and used autos. Members get 0.65% off your rate with autopay.

notes: A REDUCTION OF A RATE IS NOT A RATE. Both figures were filed as apr, and because a lower APR wins, 0.65 became the brand's advertised auto-loan rate and was ranked against a competitor's real 4.84%. The grammar is the tell: a percentage bound to 'off' is what comes off a rate. rate_discount IS rankable, against another rate_discount — 'more off is more', per the metric registry. What it must never be ranked against is the apr it was standing in for, and that is guaranteed by it being a different metric id. The corpus said unrankable and the corpus was wrong.
